replies.raw:
Here's a wild fact to start: when you type the word "unbelievable" into an AI, it doesn't see a word — it might see *three separate pieces*: `un`, `believ`, `able`.

That's because the first thing an LLM does is **tokenize** your input.

Tokenization means breaking your text into chunks called tokens — not necessarily words, but fragments the model was trained to recognize.

GPT-4 works with a vocabulary of roughly 100,000 tokens. Common words like "the" get one token. Rare words get split into several.

Here's why this matters: the sentence "I went to the bank" is just a string of tokens to the model. It has no idea yet whether "bank" means a riverbank or a financial institution — that ambiguity survives tokenization completely intact.
